evals.prompt: Riverbend Housing Alliance (nonprofit, Toledo OH, ~210 units across 4 properties) is opening a new 56-unit building, Maple Terrace, in spring. Funding is LIHTC plus HOME on 11 units and a city housing trust loan. The board wants a draft tenant selection plan to adopt at its February meeting. We'd like a preference for people experiencing homelessness and a local residency preference for Lucas County. Can you draft the TSP?
evals.expected_output: A board-ready TSP draft covering the required sections (program description with document hierarchy, eligibility, preferences with justification, application/waitlist and purge rules, screening with individualized review, income certification, reasonable accommodation, grievance/appeal, amendment clause), flagged for fair-housing legal review before adoption.
assertions: Includes the core TSP sections: program description, eligibility, preferences, application/waitlist procedures, screening criteria, income certification, reasonable accommodation, grievance/appeal, and amendment/effective date
States a hierarchy of controlling documents for when funding rules conflict
Ties each preference (homelessness, Lucas County residency) to a stated justification and flags the residency preference in particular for fair-housing/disparate-impact review
Specifies a documented waitlist purge protocol (notice, response window, documented removal)
Keeps criminal-history screening narrow and individualized (nature, severity, recency, rehabilitation) rather than a blanket ban
Recommends counsel or fair-housing review (nonprofit-housing-fair-housing) before board adoption

evals.prompt: quick q — we're a 3-property, 120-unit nonprofit landlord in Spokane and we've been self-managing but our maintenance guy quit and collections are a mess. should we hire a third-party property manager? if so what do we look for
evals.expected_output: Walks through the in-house vs third-party decision using scale, capacity, and full-cost comparison, then gives an RFP approach with a weighted scorecard, management-agreement terms to check, and an owner oversight rhythm that preserves the asset-management function.
assertions: Applies the in-house vs third-party criteria (portfolio size/scale, maintenance and collections capacity) and recommends a full-cost comparison including supervision overhead
Recommends a weighted scorecard with weights set before opening proposals
Lists management-agreement terms to check such as termination for convenience, fee structure and caps on extra fees, reporting package, and owner approval limits
Describes an ongoing oversight rhythm (monthly package review, quarterly site visits/file sampling, annual review)
Warns that the owner must keep the asset-management function and verify manager-reported occupancy and delinquency against the general ledger

evals.prompt: I'm the finance director at Hilltop Homes, a 40-unit LIHTC property we own in Asheville (year 9 of the compliance period). The roof and boilers are going to need replacing in about 4 years and our replacement reserve won't cover it. Our property manager suggested we just pull $60k from the replacement reserve this year to cover an operating shortfall from insurance increases and replenish it later. The board meets next week. What should I tell them?
evals.expected_output: Advises against using the replacement reserve for operations except where the regulatory agreement permits and then only as a board decision with a written replenishment plan; frames the issue in an asset-management plan with reserve-study reconciliation and early recapitalization planning.
assertions: Advises against funding operations from the replacement reserve, noting it is permitted only where the regulatory/loan agreement allows and should be checked there first
If considered at all, frames it as a board-level decision with a written replenishment plan
Recommends reconciling the reserve study's projected needs against the reserve balance and regulatory deposit and placing the gap in the risk register / asset-management plan
Recommends planning a recapitalization or refinancing a few years ahead rather than waiting, referring to nonprofit-housing-development-finance
Suggests modeling insurance and tax expense trends explicitly in the budget/asset-management plan
